headline: Petrol bomb hurled at Shakib Al Hasan's house in Magura
summary: Miscreants threw a cocktail and petrol bomb at the gate of the former cricket captain's residence on Wednesday night.
details: Miscreants hurled a petrol bomb and a cocktail at the gate of Shakib Al Hasan's house in Magura on Wednesday night.
The attack took place at the Keshab Mor intersection, targeting the upper part of the iron gate on the south side of the residence.
Police reported that the fire was extinguished shortly after the incident, and no major damage or injuries were reported.
A team from the Magura Sadar Police Station arrived at the scene immediately after receiving the news.
Police have deployed security personnel at the residence to ensure safety and prevent further incidents.
An investigation is underway to determine the identity of the attackers and the exact nature of the explosives used.
Shakib Al Hasan is a former MP and the former captain of the Bangladesh national cricket team.
caption:
A petrol bomb and cocktail were thrown at the gate of Shakib Al Hasan's house in Magura.

Miscreants hurled a petrol bomb and a cocktail at the gate of Shakib Al Hasan's house in Magura on Wednesday night.

The attack took place at the Keshab Mor intersection, targeting the upper part of the iron gate on the south side of the residence.

Police reported that the fire was extinguished shortly after the incident, and no major damage or injuries were reported.

A team from the Magura Sadar Police Station arrived at the scene immediately after receiving the news.

Police have deployed security personnel at the residence to ensure safety and prevent further incidents.

An investigation is underway to determine the identity of the attackers and the exact nature of the explosives used.

Shakib Al Hasan is a former MP and the former captain of the Bangladesh national cricket team.

headline_marked: Former PM's residence converted into [[July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum]]
headline: Former PM's residence converted into July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum
summary: The Ganabhaban in Dhaka has been transformed into a museum documenting the 2024 student-led uprising, featuring exhibits on torture, corruption, and the fallen.
details: The former official residence of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, known as Ganabhaban, has been officially inaugurated as the 'July 36 Mass Uprising Memorial Museum' by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
The museum is open to the public from 11 AM to 6 PM daily, except for weekends and public holidays.
The grounds feature the 'July Memorial,' a circular marble monument inscribed with the names of nearly 4,000 people killed during the last 15 years of the former regime's rule.
Various sculptures throughout the gardens depict harrowing scenes of the uprising, including bodies on rickshaws and protesters being dragged by armored vehicles.
A symbolic 'Aynaghar' (House of Mirrors) has been recreated to represent the secret prisons where victims of enforced disappearances were held.
Inside the main building, a glass-covered floor in the 'Call Room' preserves the debris and marks of the public's anger from the day the former PM fled the country.
The ground floor exhibits tools of torture, such as electric shock machines and whips, alongside evidence of corruption, illegal land allotments, and crossfire killings.
The second floor is dedicated to the July movement, showcasing personal belongings of at least 500 martyrs and other artifacts from the uprising.
caption:
From a seat of power to a memorial of resistance. The former PM's residence is now a museum of the July uprising.

The former official residence of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, known as Ganabhaban, has been officially inaugurated as the 'July 36 Mass Uprising Memorial Museum' by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

The museum is open to the public from 11 AM to 6 PM daily, except for weekends and public holidays.

The grounds feature the 'July Memorial,' a circular marble monument inscribed with the names of nearly 4,000 people killed during the last 15 years of the former regime's rule.

Various sculptures throughout the gardens depict harrowing scenes of the uprising, including bodies on rickshaws and protesters being dragged by armored vehicles.

A symbolic 'Aynaghar' (House of Mirrors) has been recreated to represent the secret prisons where victims of enforced disappearances were held.

Inside the main building, a glass-covered floor in the 'Call Room' preserves the debris and marks of the public's anger from the day the former PM fled the country.

The ground floor exhibits tools of torture, such as electric shock machines and whips, alongside evidence of corruption, illegal land allotments, and crossfire killings.

The second floor is dedicated to the July movement, showcasing personal belongings of at least 500 martyrs and other artifacts from the uprising.
